current_events: The Israel Defense Forces announces that it has assassinated Hamas militant Akram Muhammad Mahmoud Abu Machi, who took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel, during a airstrike in southern Gaza. Additionally, the Israeli Air Force and IDF publishes on X a photo of him during the October 7 onslaught
Israeli defence minister Israel Katz says Israeli forces will not withdraw from southern Lebanon even if "the United States demands it", adding that "200,000 residents will not return" to their homes
Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon

Ukrainian forces launch long-range drone strikes inside Russia, striking the Orenburg Gas Processing Plant, which also houses the only helium plant in Russia, and also striking two Russian Satellite Communications Company facilities, including one in Moscow Oblast and another in Vladimir Oblast. Russia says its forces have shot down 323 Ukrainian drones overnight
Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
Ukrainian missiles strike two Russian military airfields and several air defence systems in Crimea

The Sudan Doctors Network reports that more than 215 civilians have died at the RSF-Run Daqris Prison in Sudan's South Darfur state from the spread of diseases and epidemics, as well as torture and mistreatment of detainees
War crimes during the Sudanese civil war
Global oil prices fall to their lowest level since February 27, the day before the war started on February 28. Additionally, brent crude futures drop to US$73.50 a barrel
Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
A wildfire burns over 350 acres and destroys a home in Garfield County, Colorado, U.S., prompting evacuations

The Cottonwood Fire burns over 59,000 acres near the Eagle Point Resort in Beaver, Utah, U.S., with Governor Spencer Cox saying it is the "most destructive fire in the state’s history". Additionally, a video shows a cabin at Eagle Point being destroyed completely by the wildfire

After the deadly fire in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India, that killed 15 people, authorities across the state close down 59 coaching institutes found to be violating fire safety standards as part of a statewide enforcement drive
Five people are killed and 20 injured after an under-construction warehouse collapses in West Bengal, India

The U.S. military will require recruits to take the influenza vaccine amidst a influenza outbreak at the Lackland Air Force Base in Bexar County, Texas, U.S. The move comes after U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth lifted the military vaccine mandate
Yabloko deputy leader Maxim Kruglov is convicted and will face seven years in prison over his anti-war stance on social media, including remarks about the Russian Army
Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war
Historic Pact's candidate Iván Cepeda concedes defeat in the presidential election won by Abelardo de la Espriella
2026 Colombian presidential election

The United States Army confirms that General Chris Donahue, the commanding general of United States Army Europe and Africa, will step down on July 2, following a report by The Atlantic that he is being pressured by secretary of defense Pete Hegseth
